The voice-AI surface has three layers sold separately: (a) Exotel VoiceBot, a prompt-built LLM agent with its own console (voicebot.in.exotel.com India / voicebot.sg.exotel.com Singapore) attached to calls through an App Bazaar 'Voicebot' applet or the Connect API; (b) AgentStream, a bring-your-own-bot WebSocket stream (plus StreamKit Cloud SIP bridge and SIP trunking) for third-party bots; (c) Harmony, the contact-centre layer with 'Monitored Bot' human-in-the-loop supervision, AI Assist, CQA and CCDP.

VoiceBot builder flow per the docs: describe the bot in a prompt (optionally attach PDF/DOCX/TXT or MP3/WAV/M4A call recordings, 100 MB) -> 'Build Bot' generates Identity / Objective / Behaviour -> Configuration tab (language, voice) -> Advanced tab (versions). claim: Human-in-the-loop is a productised layer ('Monitored Bot'): a Monitoring Agent role watches live bot sessions with live transcript, AI summary and a sentiment pill; 'Sentiment Crash' and 'Bot Repetition Loop' raise critical alerts; 'Barge' disconnects the bot and connects the agent; capacity rules are 'Attention Span' and 'Agent Reserve'; overflow goes to a live queue in business hours or a callback outside them. Exotel MCP server (mcp.exotel.com, open source github.com/exotel/ExotelMCP, Java/Spring) lets an AI client create bots by natural language: the repo defines 131 MCP tools, 46 of them for VoiceBot and its Tools Server, including exotel_voicebot_create (async bot generation), place_call, assistant_update_prompt / push_version / create_multiagent, persona_*, tts_list_providers/voices, specialization_* and a Tools Server (tenants, OpenAPI-defined tools with versions and tests, data tables, knowledge corpora). Maturity signals are mixed: VoiceBot docs carry 'Coming Soon' items (templates, prompt enhancer, web call); the Sept 2026 release post lists fixes for 10 s dead air on slow TTS handshakes, ~29 s dead calls from voice/language mismatch, distorted sped-up recordings, outcomes mislabelled 'completed by bot', duplicate rows, and long-range report failures; a 'call evaluator + recommender agent' is still in testing.

claim: AgentStream WebSocket protocol (docs): Exotel->bot events connected/start/media/dtmf/mark/stop; bot->Exotel media/mark/clear (mark and clear on the bidirectional Voicebot path only); base64 16-bit little-endian mono linear PCM at 8 kHz default, with 16 or 24 kHz on request (Exotel's latency post says these are upsampled from the 8 kHz phone leg); chunks 3,200-100,000 bytes in multiples of 320; max session 60 minutes. The doc's example ids use Twilio-style placeholders (MZ.../CA.../AC...), but real Exotel CallSids are 32-hex and AccountSids are names.

Answering-machine detection exists outside the contact centre: a Beta Voice API AMD (docs.exotel.com, createdAt 2026-06-15) enabled by the account manager returns AnsweredBy (HUMAN/MACHINE/NOTSURE/NA) and AmdCause on Leg 2 in the terminal StatusCallback, asynchronously about 3-5 s after answer, and not in reports or the dashboard; ExoML create-a-leg has amd_enable and async_amd with an amd_result_success event. A bot on the ExoML Legs path could therefore get AMD, but only after it has already been streaming for ~3-5 s, and no doc shows AMD on Connect Voice AI, Campaigns v2 or the Voicebot applet.

Opt-out suppression is not entirely left to the buyer: the ECC contact centre has a tenant-level DNC list ('They will not dial through any of the campaign or queues created under that tenant from Auto-Dial'), a process-level DNC tab for voice campaigns, and dispositions that can remove a number from an outbound dialer list ('Do Not Call'). Nothing equivalent is documented for Campaigns v2 or the VoiceBot path, where the docs only advise removing opt-outs by hand.

Exotel's docs disagree on campaign scheduling: the Campaigns v2 scheduling guide offers one absolute send_at/end_at window with no recurrence, the calling-hours FAQ says Exotel 'does not automatically enforce calling hour restrictions at the API level', the Outbound Dialer guide lists a dashboard 'Daily window' (9:00 AM - 9:00 PM) and 'Days of week' setting, and ECC Lead Management has per-lead daily Time Window slots outside which the lead is disabled for dialing.

The ECC contact centre (whose web app hosts the VoiceBot console) ships as a container stack listed in its patch release notes: appserver, appserverui, asrouting, ccdp, chat-service, cms, crm-connector, customer-fetcher, data-engine, eureka, gateway, ingress-nginx-controller, interaction-service, kafka-connect, ksqldb, schema-registry, citus/postgresql 18, redis (Sentinel and Modules), scheduler, superset, fluentd and others, all pulled from bom.ocir.io (Oracle Cloud Infrastructure Registry, Mumbai; 296 references across the release notes). Inferred: a Kubernetes, Spring-Cloud-and-Kafka microservice stack distributed through OCI Mumbai. Unknown: whether Exotel's ECC SaaS runs on OCI or AWS.
